title: Does Changing 72 DPI to 300 DPI Make a Photo Sharper?
description: Changing a photo from 72 DPI to 300 DPI without resampling changes its nominal print size, not its captured detail or pixel count.
direct: Changing 72 DPI to 300 DPI can change the file’s stated print size. Sharpness depends on how many pixels you actually have for the chosen paper size.
figureAlt: Two PPI settings refer to the same single photograph and pixel grid.

cards.choice.heading: Pixels and print size are linked
cards.choice.body: A 1800 × 1200 pixel image at 300 pixels per inch describes a 6 × 4 inch print. The same pixels at 72 pixels per inch describe 25 × about 16.7 inches. Neither metadata setting adds information to the image.
sections.explain.heading: Resampling is a different operation
sections.explain.body: Resampling adds or removes pixels. Enlarging can make a grid larger without recreating fine detail that the camera never captured. Cropping also changes the pixels available for the final print, so inspect composition and size together.
sections.practice.heading: Use the correct feature
sections.practice.body: Advanced print-size fitting offers three successful free exports before Pro; basic DPI edits never use that allowance. DPI-only edits preserve image data when format, color and location are kept. Resizing or conversion can re-save the image, and re-saved files do not preserve HDR gain maps. Keep the original and inspect a print proof for important work.
faqs.reader-question-1.heading: Can the same file be marked 300 DPI without becoming a bigger file?
faqs.reader-question-1.body: Yes, a density-only edit can keep the same pixel grid. Other changes, such as resizing or format conversion, can create a different file.
faqs.reader-question-2.heading: Why does the print service still warn about low resolution?
faqs.reader-question-2.body: It may be checking the pixels left after cropping at the requested print size. Check the final crop or choose a smaller print.

steps.step-1.text: Open the photo in DPI: Photo Print Prep and inspect its pixel dimensions. Decide whether you need a DPI-only change or a specific print size.
steps.step-2.text: For a metadata-only adjustment, keep pixels and the relevant format, color and location settings unchanged. Basic single-photo DPI changes are free.
steps.step-3.text: Read back the exported pixels, both DPI axes and physical size. Confirm the print service’s requirements and scaling settings before ordering.
